ingredients.name: Vitamin A
ingredients.shortDesc:
Found in: Carrots, Green leafy vegetables and Eggs

Form: Retinol palmitate

Amount: 510 mcg

Our paediatricians say: Around here we have a saying: Vitamin A keeps the eye-doctors away! And yet it’s amongst the most common deficiencies in preschool children, affecting 62% of children. For 100% health, we give you 100% of the recommended serving!

ingredients.name: Vitamin D3
ingredients.shortDesc:
Found in: Fish, mushrooms, cheese, egg yolks etc.

Form: Cholecalciferol (vegetarian source lichen)

Amount: 600 IU

 Our paediatricians say: Vitamin D3 is a very underrated mineral for growing children. Your teen may grow out of their clothes, but they'll never grow out of good old natural minerals. For parents with fussy children - slip our supplements into their chocolate milk, they'll never know!

ingredients.name: Vitamin C
ingredients.shortDesc:
Found in: Oranges, Amla, strawberry etc.

Form: Ascorbic acid

Amount: 20 mg

Our paediatricians say: Vitamin C can stop bruises to the knee! Vitamin C helps form and repair red blood cells, bones, and tissues. In addition, vitamin C helps cuts and wounds heal, boosts the immune system, and keeps infections at bay.

ingredients.name: Vitamin B12
ingredients.shortDesc:
Found in: Fish, meats, milk, egg yolk etc.

Form: Cyanocobalamin

Amount: 2.2 mcg

Our paediatricians says: Vitamin B12 is our supermineral. It turns food into energy, which in turn fuels overall health and development. Most natural B12 is found in animal sources and this is especially good for vegetarians and vegans! As a supermineral, we supply 100% of the recommended serving.

ingredients.name: Vitamin B9
ingredients.shortDesc:
Found in: Spinach, Kiwi, Nuts, Egg yolk, etc.

Form: Dietary folate

Amount: 102 mcg

Our paediatricians say: Folates are important for several functions in the brain and body including the proper formation of the nervous system. Our product supplies approx. 75% of Vitamin B9 RDA per serving.

ingredients.name: Zinc
ingredients.shortDesc:
Found in: Meat, Legumes, Milk, Eggs, etc.

Form: Zinc citrate

Amount: 1 mg

Our paediatricians say: Zinc is one of those rare minerals that’s great all around for your child’s health, including their attention span, motor development, height and weight. Move aside, energy drinks! There’s a new hero on the block.

ingredients.name: Curcumin
ingredients.shortDesc:
Found in: Turmeric

Form: Curcumin

Amount: 5 mg

Our paediatricians say: Curcumin is anti-inflammatory, anti-allergic and antioxidant. It’s great for your child’s immune system, naturally sourced, and can be mixed into anything!

ingredients.name: DHA
ingredients.shortDesc:
Found in: Flaxseed

Form: Docosahexaenoic Acid (DHA)

Amount: 15 mg

Our paediatricians say: If there was a nutritional hero, it would be DHA. DHA is vital to the structure of the brain and may improve learning, memory, immunity and inflammation. Vegetarians are especially deficient in DHA. Our supplement is vegan and is sourced from flaxseed.

ingredients.name: Fruits and Vegetables Antioxidant blend
ingredients.shortDesc: Our paediatricians say:Our multivitamin includes a blend of 6 organic fruits and veggies, including Pomegranate, Strawberry, Apple, Beetroot, Spinach, and Carrot. Great vitamins start with real food.

faqs.question: What age range is Little Joys Multivitamin gummies suitable for?
faqs.answer: Multivitamin gummies are suitable for every child of age 13 years & above.

faqs.question: How many gummies are there in one pack of Little Joys Multivitamin Gummies?
faqs.answer: A single pack of Little Joys Multivitamin Gummies contain 30 gummies for Rs. 499.

faqs.question: Can I book a Nutritionist Consultation for my child on Little Joys?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can book an appointment with our expert nutritionist from home page. Our panel of 30+ nutritionists has helped 50k+ parents find a solution to their child’s immunity & nutritional intake concerns.

faqs.question: How many gummies should my child eat every day?
faqs.answer: We recommend one gummy a day. Each gummy has been created to help fill daily nutritional gaps and includes the highest-quality nutrients available in forms that your body prefers and can easily digest.

faqs.question: For how long does my child need to take multivitamin gummies?
faqs.answer: We recommend taking Little Joys Multivitamin Gummies for 3 months to see results.

faqs.question: Do Little Joys Multivitamin Gummies contain sugar?
faqs.answer: Little Joys Multivitamin Gummies have zero added sugar.

faqs.question: Are Multivitamin Gummies better than multivitamin syrups or other forms of multivitamin?
faqs.answer: Little Joys Multivitamin Gummies contain the same amount of nutrients as a multivitamin tablet or syrup. However, our teddy-bear shaped gummies make the process more fuss-free to get your fussy-eater to eat nutrients in a tasty and fun manner.

faqs.question: What if my child has more than 1 gummy a day?
faqs.answer: While we recommend eating 1 gummy a day, there is no medical issue with eating more than 1 gummy a day.

faqs.question: My child has a balanced diet and eats everything. Should I still give multivitamin gummies?
faqs.answer: Our primary aim is for teens to  receive all the required vitamins and nutrients necessary for their immunity. This can be through diet but more often than not because of the busy schedules & eating habits for teens, it becomes problematic to make them eat a well-balanced diet. Further, what we may think is a well-balanced diet may miss some essential vitamins and nutrients. Little joys multivitamin gummies ensure that all the necessary vitamins and nutrients are given to your child in an easy manner.

faqs.question: Are these vitamins allergen free?
faqs.answer: All Little Joys supplements are allergen-friendly and free of most common allergens - milk, eggs, shellfish, soy, gluten, wheat, fish allergens, peanuts and tree nut allergens (brazil, cashew, coconut, hazelnut, pecan, pistachio, macadamia). We're also gluten-free and non-GMO, without synthetic colors, artificial flavors or sweeteners.

faqs.question: Is your multivitamin appropriate for boys and girls?
faqs.answer: Yes. Experts suggest that boys and girls have similar nutritional needs throughout childhood and through their mid-teens. Please consult your paediatrician where appropriate.

faqs.question: What time should I give my child multivitamins?
faqs.answer: There is no specific time. We suggest your child takes one vitamin per day after a meal.

faqs.question: Are these gummies bad for my child's teeth?
faqs.answer: Little Joys Gummies are made with natural sweeteners and contain no added sugars, making them a healthier choice than regular gummies. However, like all gummies, they can stick to teeth and may contribute to cavities if good oral hygiene isn't followed. For best dental health, don't give more than 1-2 gummies in a day and encourage your child to brush or rinse their mouth after eating.
